newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares down in post-bourse as dollar slips.
newsitem.headline: German shares down in post-bourse as dollar slips.

text.p: German shares slipped in late electonic dealings as a weaker dollar weighed on German export stocks and data released on Wednesday dashed any hopes of a near-term cut in interest rates.

"Before the Ifo and M3 data everything was looking really positive, but now there's a bit of inflation fear," said one Munich dealer. "Also the fact that the dollar has fallen below the 1.50 mark level is causing some people to take profits."
The IBIS DAX, measuring all-day electronic dealings in the 30 blue chip DAX index, was down 16.35 points, or 0.59 percent, at 2,765.19 points by 1700 GMT, below the bourse close of 2,774.50.

The respected German Ifo economics institute reported a sharp rise in business confidence in October, while the Bundesbank said M3 money supply growth stayed at 8.4 percent in October, well above its 1996 target of four to seven percent.
Both figures pointed towards a recovery in the German economy, sparking some fear of inflation and weighing on both the German bond and stock markets.

Bourse trade had ended firmer after a record overnight close on Wall Street, but dealers said they expected the market to move sideways or downwards in the coming days as the impact of the Ifo and M3 data is compounded by a weaker dollar.
Although the day's most heavily traded stock was Deutsche Telekom, volumes in the telecommunications giant began to decline and other stocks grabbed a share of the spotlight.

Almost nine millon Telekom shares traded in computer IBIS dealings and over four million in bourse trade, significantly less than a total of nearly a 100 million shares which changed hands Monday and Tuesday.
Computer dealings have been temporarily extended by two hours to accomodate the additional volume.
Telekom was down 15 pfennigs at 31.85 marks in late IBIS as investors continued to take profits.

The DAX's worst performer was industrial group Preussag AG, which fell almost six percent after the company said profits for the business year that ended on September 30 fell sharply from the previous year.
Preussag shares were down 22.20 marks to 354.20 marks in late IBIS dealings.
Amongst the medium capitalised stocks, speciality chemicals firm SKW Trostberg, pharmaceuticals group Merck KGaA and tyre maker Continental were all higher after their respective nine month figures.
In late IBIS trade SKW was up 1.75 marks at 43 marks, Merck rose 1.45 marks to 56.55 marks and Continental gained 93 pfennigs to 26.62 marks.

Meanwhile, shares in metals and trading group Metallgesellschaft resumed trade up 50 pfennigs at 28 marks, after the trade was suspended following the announcement of the sale of the firms banking operations.
